rows.question: RTI ka jawab nahi aaya to appeal kahan karni hai
queries: RTI ka jawab nahi aaya to appeal kahan karni hai
Right to Information Act appeal to first appellate authority non receipt of information
Right to Information Act section 19 appeal
Right to Information Act section 7 disposal of request time limit
topSources: The Right to Information Act, 2005 s19

rows.answer:
An appeal against the failure to give a response to a request for information within the time specified shall lie to an officer who is senior in rank to the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, in each public authority, as provided under Section 19 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 [1][12].

Conditions and time limits:
- The appeal must be preferred within thirty days from the expiry of the period specified under Section 7, as stated in Section 19 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 [1].
- The officer may admit the appeal after the expiry of thirty days if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal in time, under Section 19 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 [1].

rows.question: Someone cheated people online using my password. What is the punishment, and how do I prove the messages in court?
queries: Someone cheated people online using my password. What is the punishment, and how do I prove the messages in court?

Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 section 61 63 admissibility of electronic records and digital evidence
topSources: The INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2000 Amendment s66C
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Draft stage of translated version) s?
rows.answer: Whoever commits identity theft by fraudulently or dishonestly making use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh, under Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, 2000 [1]. Furthermore, whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, under Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000 [4]. Additionally, whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine under Section 318(4)

rows.question: A company's director signed a cheque that bounced. Is the director personally liable, and can it also be cheating?
queries: A company's director signed a cheque that bounced. Is the director personally liable, and can it also be cheating?
director personal liability for dishonour of cheque company offence Negotiable Instruments Act
Negotiable Instruments Act section 138 offence by companies director liability

topSources: The Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978 s6
The Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act, 2017 s8
rows.answer:
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 makes a drawer liable for a dishonoured cheque, and Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 provides that if the person committing an offence under section 138 is a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence [1][3]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- The cheque must be presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier [1].
- The payee or the holder in due course must make a demand for payment by giving a notice in writing to the drawer within thirty days of the receipt of information from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid [1].
- The drawer must fail to make the payment to the payee or holder in due course within fifteen days of the receipt of the notice [1].

Related provisions:
- Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 covers offences by companies [3].

rows.question: Is a contract signed by a 16 year old valid, and can a child be punished for a crime?
queries: Is a contract signed by a 16 year old valid, and can a child be punished for a crime?
Indian Contract Act section 11 competency to contract age of majority minor agreement void
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita section 26 nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita section 82 act of a child above seven and under twelve of immature understanding
topSources: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Draft stage of translated version) s?
rows.answer:
A contract signed by a 16-year-old is not valid because every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 [1].

A child under seven years of age cannot be punished for a crime because nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age, under Section 20 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the old law Section 82 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [5][10]. Furthermore, nothing is an offence which is done by a child above seven years of age and under twelve years of age who has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge of the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion, under Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the old law Section 83 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [6].

rows.answer:
Yes, a wife who is unable to maintain herself can get monthly maintenance from her husband if he has sufficient means and neglects or refuses to maintain her, as provided under Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) [1][8][12]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- The wife must be unable to maintain herself [1].
- The husband must have sufficient means and must neglect or refuse to maintain her [1].
- An application for interim maintenance and proceedings expenses shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice of the application [1].
- An application to levy and recover any amount due under the order must be made to the court within a period of one year from the date on which it became due [1].

Related provisions:
- Section 145 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 covers "Procedure" and specifies the districts where proceedings may be taken, evidence recording, and ex parte hearings [3].

Regarding punishment, if a person ordered to pay maintenance fails without sufficient cause to comply with the order, the Magistrate may issue a warrant

rows.question: Does the limitation period apply to arbitration, and how long do I have to file a suit for a loan I gave?
queries: Does the limitation period apply to arbitration, and how long do I have to file a suit for a loan I gave?
limitation period applicability to arbitration proceedings
Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 section 43 limitation
Limitation Act 1963 schedule article 19 money lent suits limitation period
topSources: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 s43
The Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 s43
rows.answer:
The Limitation Act, 1963 shall apply to arbitrations as it applies to proceedings in court under Section 43 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 [1].

For a suit for money payable for money lent, the period of limitation is three years under Article 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and the period begins to run when the loan is made [5]. For a like suit when the lender has given a cheque for the money, the period of limitation is three years under Article 20 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and the period begins to run when the cheque is paid [6]. For money lent under an agreement that it shall be payable on demand, the period of limitation is three years under Article 21 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and the period begins to run when the loan is made [7]. Any suit for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere in the schedule has a period of limitation of three years under Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1963, beginning to run when the right to sue accrues [4].

Conditions and time limits:
- For arbitration under Section 43 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitration shall be deemed to have commenced on the date referred to in Section 21 [1].

rows.answer:
In Miranda v. Arizona, the US Supreme Court considered whether an accused person must be apprised of their right not to answer and keep silent while being interrogated by the police [12]. The Court observed that if a person in custody is to be subjected to interrogation, they must first be informed in clear and unequivocal terms that they have the right to remain silent, noting that such a warning is an absolute prerequisite in overcoming the inherent pressures of the interrogation atmosphere [12]. The Court further observed that the warning of the right to remain silent must be accompanied by the explanation that anything said may be used against the person [12].

rows.question: Shop sold me a defective phone and won't replace it, where do I complain?
queries: Shop sold me a defective phone and won't replace it, where do I complain?
consumer dispute redressal commission jurisdiction complaint defective goods
The Consumer Protection Act 2019 section 34 district commission jurisdiction
The Consumer Protection Act 2019 section 35 manner in which complaint shall be made
rows.answer:
The District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed one crore rupees, under Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [1]. Under Section 11 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, the District Forum has jurisdiction where the value of goods or services and compensation claimed does not exceed rupees twenty lakhs [4].

Conditions and time limits:
- A complaint may be instituted in a District Commission within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the opposite party or each of the opposite parties ordinarily resides, carries on business, has a branch office, or personally works for gain, or where the cause of action wholly or in part arises, or where the complainant resides or personally works for gain, under Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [1].
- Under Section 11 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, a complaint may be instituted within the local limits where the opposite party actually and voluntarily resides, carries on business, has a branch office, or personally works for gain, or where the cause of action wholly or in part arises [4].
